title: Subtle Domain Restrictions in Radical Compositions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let u(x) = x^2 and v(x) = sqrt(x). Form the composition (u o v)(x) and determine its natural domain, contrasting it with the domain of the simplified formula.

steps.title: Find the Domain of the Inner Function
steps.explanation: Any input x to the composite function u(v(x)) must first be eligible to enter the inner function v. Because the square root requires non-negative radicands, x must satisfy x >= 0.
steps.why: The input to a composite function must lie in the domain of the first function evaluated.

steps.title: Evaluate the Composition Expression
steps.explanation: For any non-negative number x, squaring the principal square root returns x.
steps.why: Definition of the principal square root function for non-negative real numbers.

steps.title: Establish the True Composite Domain
steps.explanation: Although the simplified formula y = x appears defined on all of R, the composite function cannot accept negative numbers because v(x) would fail to evaluate in the real number system.
steps.why: Domain constraints established by inner functions cannot be erased by subsequent algebraic cancellation.
